medium_value.description: Reconcile the preflight decision logic between D-1.1 and D-1.4. §1.2.1 says `estimated_input > ceiling → preempt (unchanged)`, but §1.2.4 says an uncalibrated entry is never preempted from the heuristic alone while `estimate ≤ ceiling × 1.05`. Define one decision table in §1.2.1 with explicit bands (≤ probed → proceed; probed < e ≤ ceiling → warn; ceiling < e ≤ 1.05×ceiling and uncalibrated and heuristic-only → warn; otherwise preempt), and make `test_ceiling_policy.py` assert every band including the 1.05 edge.

State that `isReasoningClass` resolves aliases to catalog ids before the `GENERATED_REASONING[modelId]` lookup, since `DEFAULTS.model` becomes the alias `opus` and persona headers use aliases. Add a test case with an alias input.

Enumerate the normalisation rules beyond `failure_mode` and let the three KF-004 fixtures determine coverage: severity case-folding, category enum mapping, id-format repair, and array-vs-string coercion. Also list `failure_mode_derived` (and any other added field) in the envelope-schema additive changes alongside `rejected_summary`.

Specify sanitisation for `rejected_summary[].description_head` and `title`: strip control characters and markdown heading/fence markers, cap length, and apply the same at render time in the `## Rejected dissent payloads` section.

Tighten the `verdict-derive.sh` check: define which envelope is selected when a sprint has multiple review rounds (latest by mtime or by `round` field), and require that each `rejected_summary` item's `anchor` or `title` appears in the section, not merely the heading.

Make the instruction diet concrete: list the protocols that move to `.claude/protocols/reference/`, list the ~1,000 B removed from `CLAUDE.loa.md` to reach 9,216 B, and add a grep gate (in `check-prompt-budget.sh` or a bats case) that no `@`-import, skill include, or script path references a moved protocol without the one-line pointer.

Define the determinism of the replay A/B gate: state whether `run_replay.sh` uses recorded model responses or live calls; if live, specify the number of repetitions and a tolerance (or a McNemar-style comparison) instead of 'a recall drop on any gold case blocks the sprint'.

Derive the Flatline model-id allowlist from `generated-model-maps.sh` rather than hand-maintained regexes. If a regex must remain, note that `^gpt-[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-codex|-pro)?$` excludes ids without a minor version (`gpt-5`) and any `o*`/`codex-*` ids the catalog may serve.

Map the provider's 'prompt too long' / beta-required 400 response to a named cheval error class with a remediation hint (set `params.beta_headers`, run calibration, or `LOA_CHEVAL_LEGACY_CEILING=1`) so Open Question 1 resolves mechanically on the first large call.

Specify `beta_headers` join semantics (comma-join, deduplicated against any beta values the adapter already sets for thinking or other features), state applicability to the Bedrock/Vertex adapters, and add a unit test — §7 has none for D-1.2.

Make the D-4.4 probe recorder write-once (skip when `.run/.active-skill-probe` exists) and wrap it so any failure is non-fatal to `implement-gate.sh`; add a test that every `agent:` value in SKILL.md frontmatter appears in `.claude/data/agent-types.yaml` (unknown type fails lint).

Fix the ceiling formula for 200K entries so input + resolved max_tokens never exceeds the context window. With D-1.3 raising the default output to min(64,000, max_output) the probed floor of 180,000 yields 180,000 + 64,000 = 244,000 > 200,000 for Haiku 4.5/4.x entries (Appendix A). Replace `max(probed_ceiling, context_window − max_output_tokens)` with a per-request check `estimated_input + resolved_max_tokens ≤ context_window` (clamp `max_tokens` down before preempting), and keep `probed_ceiling` only as the warn threshold, not as a value that can raise the hard ceiling.

Order Sprint 1 so the ceiling helper and generator changes (D-1.1, generated maps) land before their consumers (D-1.5, D-1.6), or split FR-1 into a Python half and a TS/bash half. Move the migration notes for the temperature and `max_tokens` default changes into Sprint 1 rather than the Sprint 4 addendum.

Name the SessionStart hook that writes `.run/context-class` (extend `loa-run-state-surface.sh`, which already parses the payload, rather than adding a hook) and state how a mid-session model switch is handled (file is advisory; `/loa` re-derives from the current model when available).

Name and justify the magic constants: the 20,000-token Bridgebuilder headroom (`maxInput = derivedCeiling − 20_000`), the 0.9×ceiling count trigger, and `BB_OUTPUT_CAP = 32_000`; expose each as a tested constant.

State explicitly whether the ceiling formula applies to Bedrock/Vertex Anthropic entries (§1.2.1 says 'every Anthropic HTTP entry'). If excluded, say they keep `probed_ceiling`; if included, note that platform context windows may differ from the direct API and the formula uses each entry's own `context_window`.
Add a risk row for rate limiting on 1M-class requests (input-tokens-per-minute 429s) with the retry/backoff class and the ledger fields that record it.

Add a schema-conformance test that validates fixture envelopes carrying the new additive fields (`rejected_summary`, `input_ceiling`, `companion_voice`, `failure_mode_derived`) against the updated trajectory schema.
Require the new bats suites (companion voice, normaliser, flatline max-tokens, implement-gate probe) to run against an isolated `.run` directory and ledgers, per the KF-033 pollution finding.

Make companion-voice selection compatible with the parallel execution claimed in §9. Choose the companion family from the primary chain's configured first entry (known before any call) rather than from 'the primary chain's first success', or run both family chains concurrently and drop one post hoc. Add an explicit rule for same-family collision after cross-family fallback (e.g. primary chain lands on `claude-headless` and the companion is also Anthropic): record `voices_dropped` with reason `same_family` or re-route the companion.

Add a cost guard for the newly reachable size band. Raising the ceiling from 180,000 to 872,000 removes the de-facto per-call cost cap; specify that the warn/preempt gate consults the cycle-125 budget preflight/breaker with a pre-call cost estimate computed from `estimated_input × input_price + resolved_max_tokens × output_price`, records `estimated_cost` in the `input_ceiling` envelope object, and that a configurable per-call ceiling (or the breaker) can preempt independently of token count.

Define the calibration write-back path. The formula and tests branch on `calibrated_at`, but nothing in the SDD sets it. Specify the command (e.g. the existing probe tool with `--write-calibration`) that writes `calibrated_at`, the calibrated `value`, and an evidence pointer into `ceiling_calibration`, and optionally an auto-calibration rule (N successful calls above `probed_ceiling` recorded in `.run/model-invoke.jsonl` promotes `probed_ceiling`).

Specify how the ceiling exists 'in one place' across three runtimes. `loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py` cannot be imported by `flatline-orchestrator.sh` or `gen-bb-registry.ts`. State that `gen-adapter-maps.sh` and `gen-bb-registry.ts` either invoke the Python helper at generation time or that the helper emits a JSON sidecar consumed by both generators, and add a parity test asserting `generated-model-maps.sh`, `truncation.generated.ts`, and the Python helper agree per entry.

State the generator change needed for D-1.6: `gen-adapter-maps.sh` must emit a new `MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT` (and ceiling) map into `generated-model-maps.sh`, since the bash orchestrator has no other way to read `max_output_tokens`. Alternatively drop the explicit `--max-tokens` in `call_model` and rely on cheval's D-1.3 default, which computes the same `min(64000, max_output)`.

Analyse and test the interplay between the new default `max_tokens` (4,096 → 64,000) and the cycle-125 budget/pricing preflight. If the pre-call reservation is computed from `max_tokens`, every call now reserves ~16× more output cost and may trip the breaker on ordinary calls. Specify whether reservation uses `max_tokens` or a historical average, and add a test that a nominal review call does not trip the breaker under default budgets.

Harden the `count_tokens` path: bound the call with an explicit timeout (e.g. 10 s), record `estimate_source: heuristic|counted` and `count_latency_ms` in the `input_ceiling` envelope object, and cache the counted value per request so fallback-chain retries do not re-issue the count.

Add the design for `deriveTimeoutMs` in Bridgebuilder. §7 lists `timeout.test.ts (deriveTimeoutMs for the 5-family)` but §1.2.5 does not say how the timeout changes with `maxOutput` up to 32,000 or with `reasoning: true`. Specify the formula (base + per-output-token factor × reasoning multiplier) and its clamp.

blockers.concern: A 4.8× input ceiling increase (180K → 872K) ships default-on with zero measured calls on this account. The 1M window is 'assumed GA' (PRD appendix, Open Question 1); historically Anthropic's 1M context has been beta-header and usage-tier gated. The 'warn' action is not a mitigation in autonomous /run mode where nobody reads WARN lines; the failure moves from a cheap, fast `preempt` with a specific exit code to a post-upload provider 400, after which the fallback chain (D-2.1 walks chains 'as today') re-sends the same oversized payload to the next model.
blockers.why_matters: If the assumption is wrong, every large review/audit becomes api_failure across the whole chain, verdicts degrade, wall time and egress are wasted per voice, and the evidence trail (KF-017/KF-011 shapes) points at the provider rather than the catalog. The design's own §6 says fail-closed 'where today' but this is precisely the place where today is fail-closed and tomorrow is not.
blockers.recommendation: Invert the default: an uncalibrated entry uses probed_ceiling; the derived ceiling unlocks only after the probe tool writes `calibrated_at` (make that write part of sprint 1 and run it once on this account). Treat provider 'prompt too long' / context-length 400s as non-retryable across the fallback chain (do not re-send the same payload to the next voice). Keep `warn` for the calibrated-but-heuristic-uncertain band only.

blockers.concern: The ceiling formula for 200K-class entries is internally inconsistent with the new output default. D-1.1 computes 200,000 − 64,000 = 136,000 for Haiku 4.5 and the 4.x/Bedrock entries, then discards it in favour of max(probed 180,000, derived). D-1.3 simultaneously raises the default wire max_tokens for those same entries from 4,096 to 64,000 (streaming). Anthropic's API rejects requests where input_tokens + max_tokens exceeds the context window (400 'prompt is too long'), so every request in the 136K–180K input band that used to succeed with a 4,096 default will now fail deterministically at the provider, after upload, on the exact models the SDD says 'remain available by detection or override' — including the Bedrock compliance path (KF-016 prefer_bedrock).
blockers.why_matters: The probed 180,000 was measured with a small max_tokens; it is not a property of the model independent of output size. Shipping max(probed, cw − mot) into the shared ceiling.py helper propagates a wrong invariant to cheval, Flatline and Bridgebuilder at once, and the failure mode (post-upload 400 → api_failure voice → degraded verdict) is the KF-017 shape that is hard to attribute.
blockers.recommendation: Define ceiling = context_window − resolved_wire_max_tokens − thinking_budget (if any) and never take max() with a probed value measured under different output settings. Add a second preflight invariant `estimate + max_tokens ≤ context_window` that auto-shrinks max_tokens (with a recorded note) before preempting. Extend test_input_size_consumers.py with a 170K input on a 200K entry under the new 64K default and assert it is not sent as-is.

blockers.concern: The ceiling formula uses max(probed_ceiling, context_window - max_output_tokens), which can exceed the declared residual input capacity for 200K models when max_output_tokens is large.
blockers.why_matters: For entries like Haiku 4.5, the document explicitly chooses 180K even though 200K - 64K is 136K, creating a possible total-token envelope of 244K. This can cause provider rejection or output truncation under exactly the models meant to remain safe.
blockers.recommendation: Use min(probed_ceiling, context_window - configured_output_budget) when output budget is reserved, or explicitly lower the default/requested max output when allowing 180K input on 200K models.

blockers.concern: The design assumes Anthropic 5-family 1M context is generally available while leaving the beta header unset, but the open question admits this may not be true for the operator account.
blockers.why_matters: If the account still requires a beta header or does not support the 1M window, the new derived 872K ceiling will route very large requests to a provider that rejects them, causing core review/audit workflows to fail after expensive prompt construction.
blockers.recommendation: Make the large-context capability a startup or preflight probe result before enabling derived ceilings above the probed value; require either a successful model/account capability probe or an explicit operator override before warn-and-proceed is allowed.

blockers.concern: There is no cost analysis anywhere in the SDD although every lever multiplies spend: inputs up to 872K (long-context premium pricing above 200K), default outputs 4K→64K, a second dissent voice on every review and audit, `cheap` moving from Haiku to Sonnet 5 (roughly 3–5× per token) for the scorer that runs on every dissent, and BB payloads 128K→200K. Cycle-125 built the pricing ladder, cost-report and breaker CLI; the SDD does not wire any of them to these changes.
blockers.why_matters: A single Flatline review that used to preempt at 180K can now legitimately send 800K tokens × 2 voices × N iterations plus scorer calls; the breaker thresholds were tuned for the old envelope and will either trip constantly or not at all. Cost is the operator's actual constraint and it is invisible in this design.
blockers.recommendation: Add a per-gate expected-cost table (before/after) to the SDD, add the long-context premium tier to the pricing ladder, make the `warn` band include a cost estimate and honour the breaker before sending, and set an explicit per-request cost ceiling default (kill-switchable) for dissent voices.

blockers.concern: Warn-and-proceed for uncalibrated ceilings allows heuristic estimates up to 105 percent of the derived ceiling to reach the provider without a hard bound.
blockers.why_matters: The heuristic is described as conservative but not proven. Allowing requests above the derived ceiling by estimate can create hard provider failures, excessive latency, or unexpected billing, especially for autonomous runs.
blockers.recommendation: Cap warn-and-proceed at the derived ceiling unless count_tokens succeeds; require exact token counting for requests above the probed ceiling or fail with an actionable calibration message.
